name: DiscoverPhysics
fullName: DiscoverPhysics: discovering laws of an alien physics

actions.experiment: Submit a JSON experiment: initial positions, velocities and charges of the controllable particles plus the list of measurement times; receive the simulated noisy positions and velocities.
actions.fit: Propose a candidate law with free parameters and request a least-squares fit against all trajectories logged so far; receive the fit report as text.
actions.submit_final: Submit the terminal answer: a plain-text explanation of the world's physics and a Python discovered_law function with up to five fittable parameters.

evaluation.efficiency: Among passing episodes, prefer fewer experiment/fit rounds before submitting, then lower normalized MSE.
evaluation.failure: Failure if either threshold is missed, if the submitted Python law errors or cannot be fit, or if the budget is exhausted without a final submission.
evaluation.success: The episode passes when the submitted law's parameters are fit on the agent's observed data, rolled out on the world's held-out noise-free test particles, yields per-trajectory normalized MSE below 0.1 (MSE divided by test-trajectory variance) AND the LLM judge scores the explanation at least 0.9 against the world's human-written rubric.

assignment.generation: An instance is (public world name from the 11 released worlds: gravity, yukawa, fractional, circle, three_species, dark_matter, ether, hubble, oscillator, extra_dimensions, coulomb_easy) x (integer seed), run through the official runner with the default N-body engine, max_rounds 16 and position-only noise sigma = 0.05; worlds are generated on demand by the simulator from the world definition, so the seed plus world name fully reproduces the instance.
assignment.observation: Text/JSON only: the universal mission prompt, the world-specific experiment schema, and for each submitted experiment the simulator's returned positions and velocities of the controllable particles at the requested measurement times with Gaussian observation noise (sigma = 0.05). Parameter-fit results are returned as text at the start of the next round. No force law, field equation, coupling or hidden-species information is ever revealed, and held-out test particles are never shown.
assignment.reference: Published DiscoverPhysics protocol (arXiv:2605.26087) and its open-source simulator/agent harness: rounds of agent-designed N-body experiments in a world with hidden non-canonical physics, then a final prose explanation plus Python law scored by held-out trajectory MSE and an LLM-judge rubric score. New design choices: fixed 16-round budget, (world, seed) instance keying at sigma = 0.05 position noise, the paper's 0.9 judge threshold, a thin action wrapper and explicit trajectory-logging requirements.
assignment.task: Given one DiscoverPhysics world whose force law, field equation, couplings and hidden particle species are undisclosed, design and run experiments to infer the governing law, then submit a plain-text explanation of the world's physics together with a Python implementation of the discovered law (at most five fitted free parameters).
assignment.verification: Recompute the verdict with the official scorer: scipy least-squares fit of the submitted law, rollout against the world's held-out noise-free test trajectories for normalized MSE, and the LLM judge (claude-opus-4-6) scoring the explanation against the world's rubric. Archive for both passing and failing episodes the per-run experiment-trajectory CSV, every round's submitted experiment/fit JSON and returned observation text, the final explanation and law, and the terminal metrics, so any run can be independently replayed and rescored.

otherModels.transport: Claude Code CLI (claude -p, tools disabled, one turn, JSON output)
otherModels.callsPerEpisode: one per evaluated final law (official ExplanationJudge)

notes: Hidden answers: configurations.json holds world, seed and noise settings that define the hidden physics; never show them to the player.
